paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the first bar, the lighter bar is 39.50%, and the darker bar is only 0.04%). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning on certain key principles eliminates bias to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across prompts specific to Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, also considerably reducing bias across Virtual Contact prompts.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated by a language model under three different prompt categories—“Support of Authorities,” “Extended Contact,” and “Virtual Contact”—before and after instruction tuning, categorized by the type of contact (no contact, positive contact, negative contact). The vertical axis represents “Bias Percentage,” scaled linearly from 0 to 70, with tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis lists the three prompt categories in left-to-right order. For each category, there are up to three bars: light gray for “No Contact Before,” light red for “Positive Contact Before,” and light blue for “Negative Contact Before.” Overlaid on these are darker, patterned bars representing the same conditions “After” instruction tuning: gray with diagonal stripes for “No Contact After,” red with diagonal stripes for “Positive Contact After,” and blue with diagonal stripes for “Negative Contact After.” The darker bars are stacked on top of the lighter bars, indicating the reduction in bias post-tuning. For “Support of Authorities,” the light gray bar is 39.50% with a dark gray overlay of 0.04%, the light red bar is 31.83% with no dark red overlay (0.00%), and the light blue bar is 42.38% with no dark blue overlay (0.00%). For “Extended Contact,” the light gray bar is 40.61% with no dark gray overlay (0.00%), the light red bar is 36.13% with no dark red overlay (0.00%), and the light blue bar is 47.28% with a dark blue overlay of 0.11%. For “Virtual Contact,” the light gray bar is 39.74% with a dark gray overlay of 10.00%, the light red bar is 39.17% with a dark red overlay of 10.01%, and the light blue bar is 43.83% with a dark blue overlay of 10.02%. The chart visually emphasizes that instruction tuning nearly eliminates bias for “Support of Authorities” and “Extended Contact” prompts (as indicated by the near-absence of dark bars), while reducing bias by approximately 10 percentage points for “Virtual Contact” prompts.
